paper_title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only $3$K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

sections.content: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised finetuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only 3K samples, while preserving general video generation quality. 1. Introduction Recent video generation models [1, 10, 15, 40] have made impressive strides in visual fidelity and temporal coherence, yet they remain noticeably brittle 1 when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions [2, 3, 28]. Targeted post-training has thus emerged as vital route to reinforce physical capabilities beyond pre-training [18, 32]. However, existing paradigms involve clear trade-offs: ➀ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) offers dense supervision [17, 29, 42, 49], but operates on offline data that mismatches the states visited during inference; ➁ reinforcement learning (RL) optimizes directly over onpolicy rollouts [8, 12, 14], yet suffers from sparse, illdefined rewards and credit-assignment bottlenecks. Recent ➂ on-policy distillation (OPD) [22, 34] provides natural middle ground by querying teacher for dense supervision on student-visited rollout states. Building upon this, on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) [50] further removes the need for an external teacher by casting the same model into asymmetric roles: the student acts on inference-time inputs, while the teacher accesses additional privileged context to supervise the student rollouts. The central question of OPSD therefore becomes how to leverage extra information to turn the same model into stronger self-teacher, as shown in Figure 2 (a). An effective privileged context should directly expose the information required by the target capability and reliably enhance teacher predictions on student rollout states. This principle has shown strong promise in language reasoning via ground-truth answers and rationales [31, 47, 50], as well as in image generation via target-image multimodal representations [13]. Extending this paradigm to video generation, however, is far less straightforward, as the primary bottleneck lies in modeling physically plausible dynamics, capability that also defies evaluation by standard reward models [3, 18, 42]. Yet, designing effective privileged context remains non-trivial: text expansion provides richer descriptions but remains fundamentally declarative, whereas real reference videos capture complete dynamics but heavily entangle them with irrelevant appearance, identity, and background clutter without controllable structure (Figure 2 (b)). These bottlenecks lead to our core research question:

sections.title: Research Question
sections.content: How can we construct privileged context that unlocks video generator as its own physics teacher? To answer this question, we introduce PhysOPSD, which proposes executable code as privileged physical context for video generation OPSD. Our key insight is that an executable physical scene instantiates an editable world rather than fixed visual outcome. This executability inherently provides two structural properties absent in raw video data: ❶ abstraction, the ability to express dynamics across varying information densities; and ❷ controllability, the ability to isolate and systematically perturb underlying phys- (a) OPSD shifts physFigure 2. Background overview. ical post-training from reward engineering to privileged context design; (b) Executable code explicitly parameterizes physical processes, uniquely unlocking abstraction and controllability; (c) Using executable code as privileged context, PhysOPSD internalizes physical dynamics into the student for simulation-free video generation. ical parameters. To operationalize this insight, we first develop PhysOPSD-Engine, which converts diverse real-world scenarios into verifiable simulation code and renders synchronized physical drafts via coding agent. PhysOPSD then systematically translates these two properties into OPSD: dual-level physical privilege exploits abstraction by pairing dense drafts with abstract drafts, establishing an intermediate physical information bottleneck to bridge the privilege gap and prevent appearance shortcuts; controlled physical variation exploits controllability by altering specific physical parameters across paired scenes with shared rollout noise, explicitly supervising how physical shifts dictate dynamic outcomes. By internalizing structured code privilege through on-policy selfdistillation, PhysOPSD empowers base video generators to generate more physically plausible dynamics and stable interactions directly from text prompts. To summarize, this work contributes threefold: We propose code as privileged physical context for video generation, and introduce PhysOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework incorporating dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap and controlled physical variation to capture causal dynamic shifts. We develop PhysOPSD-Engine to translate realworld physical into verifiable and scenarios controllable simulation programs, and construct PhysOPSD-3K, an executable physical scene dataset featuring multi-abstraction drafts and paired 2 physical variants. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD consistently improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming prior SFT and RL baselines with only small fraction of their training data, without compromising general generation quality. 2. Related Work On-Policy Distillation. On-policy distillation (OPD) mitigates train-test distribution shifts by supervising the student directly on its self-generated states with dense feedback [22, 34]. This paradigm has been applied to consolidate domain experts in language models such as MOPD [27], fuse visual capabilities in diffusion and flow models [7, 20], and optimize sampling trajectories in video generation [9]. To eliminate the reliance on external teachers, onpolicy self-distillation (OPSD) constructs stronger self-teacher from the same model under asymmetric privileged information [50]. While ground-truth solutions and rationales serve as privileged context in language reasoning [31, 47, 50], D-OPSD [13] employs target-image multimodal representations to tune few-step image diffusion models. For video models, OPSD-V [26] replaces older KV-cache history with real video frames to mitigate long-horizon drift in few-step autoregressive (AR) generators. Unlike OPSD-V, which focuses on causal AR cache stabilization, PhysOPSD explores on-policy self-distillation for general video generation, introducing executable code as privileged physical context. Code-for-Vision. Empowered by modern foundational vision-language models (VLMs) [33, 37], executable code is increasingly utilized for visual scene synthesis and understanding. Early efforts such as 3D-GPT [35] synthesize Blender scripts to procedurally build 3D environments [16]. Recent studies further leverage coding agents for programmatic visual reconstruction, editing, and quantitative physical reasoning [21, 36, 41, 48]. More recently, researchers have explored coding agents to assist visual generation by delegating spatiotemporal processes to code execution [6], either as physics-aware drafts in Blender [19] or cinematic previsualizations in Three.js [23]. While existing generative approaches largely seek to replace part of generative modeling with coding agent capabilities, PhysOPSD explores how executable code can empower the generative model itself. 3. The effectiveness of OPSD therefore hinges on whether the privileged context reliably improves teacher predictions on student-visited states. 4. PhysOPSD 4.1. Overview OPSD relies on privileged context that reliably improves self-teacher predictions along student rollout states. In modeling physical dynamics, however, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts remain inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos merely capture entangled visual observations. Executable Code as Privileged Context. PhysOPSD bridges this gap by introducing executable code as privileged physical context, as shown in Figure 3. 3 Figure 3. Overview of our proposed PhysOPSD. Unlike static text or video observations, an executable program explicitly specifies physical laws, object states, and dynamic parameters within an edthereby uniquely providing exitable simulation, plicit parametric control. To operationalize this, PhysOPSD-Engine first translates real-world physical references Vref into an executable program P. Simulating in backend yields visual physical draft = (P) and grounded target prompt = Describe(P, d). Here, code generates the underlying physical dynamics, while the rendered visual draft conditions the self-teacher. PhysOPSD builds Structured Physical Supervision. upon an omni video generator v𝜽 (x𝑡, 𝑡, p, d), where = denotes text-only conditioned generation. Rather than treating as static condition, PhysOPSD leverages two intrinsic properties of executable code: ❶ Abstraction: synthesizing dense drafts ddense and abstract drafts dabs to establish stepped hierarchy (ddense dabs p) that smooths the privilege gap; ❷ Controllability: perturbing physical parameters 𝝓 across paired scenes with shared rollout noise to capture causal dynamic shifts. The subsequent Section 4.2 details PhysOPSD-Engine and PhysOPSD-3K, while Sections 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 elaborate the structured self-distillation mechanisms of PhysOPSD. 4.2. Executable Physical Context Engine Reference-Guided Scene Construction. To seed simulations with natural diversity, PhysOPSD-Engine ingests real-world physical scenarios from WISA [42] and public video collections. Rather than attempting to simulate arbitrary physical phenomena, the physical scope is deliberately restricted to simulationgroundable physical dynamics, categorized into three domains: (I) rigid-body and contact dynamics, (II) elastic and deformable solid mechanics, and (III) fluid dynamics. Phenomena such as turbulent gas diffusion or thermodynamic phase shifts are excluded due to numerical instability and the difficulty of isolating causal physical parameters in standard simulators. Given reference video Vref, coding agent then extracts the dominant physical event and formulates structured physical scene specification: = (O, X0, 𝚽, E, C), (6) where defines object geometries, X0 specifies initial kinetic states, 𝚽 collects physical properties (e.g., friction, elasticity, mass), indicates interaction mechanisms, and configures the camera trajectory. The coding agent then compiles into an executable simulation program = (S). Standard simulation backends such as MuJoCo [39], Genesis [38], and Blender [4] are employed purely for their deterministic contact solvers and numerical stability, without asserting the superiority of any specific engine. Crucially, the governing principle is to reconstruct the physical scenario rather than visually reproduce the reference video: geometries and textures are simplified as long as the underlying physical mechanics are faithfully instantiated. To systematically synthesize verifiable and controllable privileged physical context, we develop PhysOPSD-Engine, an agentic pipeline that translates real-world physical references into executable scene programs and rendered physical drafts. Execution-Guided Verification. The synthesized program is then refined through an iterative execution-observation-revision loop. Rather than optimizing for pixel-level trajectory similarity to Vref, verification enforces four strict criteria: Execution validity, ensuring code executes and renders without runtime divergence; Physical validity, verifying that dynamic events emerge from simulation mechanics rather than hard-coded keyframe animations; Visual observability, confirming that primary dynamic interactions are clearly visible within the viewport; Parameter controllability, ensuring that systematically perturbing key physical parameters produces physically consistent and observable dynamic responses; Once verified, the target prompt is grounded directly on the executed outcome, = Describe(S, d), guaranteeing semantic and causal alignment across d. PhysOPSD-3K Dataset. Using PhysOPSD-Engine, we further construct PhysOPSD-3K, an executable physical scene dataset for video generation. Each sample is represented as structured tuple: D𝑖 = {p𝑖, P𝑖, d𝑖, M𝑖}, (7) where P𝑖 is the executable program, d𝑖 is the rendered visual draft, p𝑖 is the grounded prompt, and M𝑖 denotes structured metadata detailing physical parameters and execution configurations. Unlike static video collections, this executable formulation endows PhysOPSD-3K with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Encompassing the base scenes alongside their derived multi-abstraction drafts and parametercontrolled variants, PhysOPSD-3K comprises 3K total instances. We next detail how these structured properties are translated into self-distillation. 4.3. Structured Physical Self-Distillation Building upon the executable formulation, PhysOPSD further translates code abstraction into dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap, and leverages controllability via controlled physical variation to supervise causal dynamic shifts, as illustrated in Figure 4. 4.3.1. Dual-Level Physical Privilege Directly distilling from dense physical draft ddense to text-only student may incur two fundamental obstacles: (i) an excessively wide privilege gap that impedes knowledge internalization, and (ii) the risk of geometric shortcuts where the teacher overfits to explicit geometry rather than abstracting causal dynamics. We thus introduce an abstract physical draft dabs as an intermediate physical information bottleneck, isolating motion and contact topology while filtering out fine-grained visual details. Figure 4. Case study on physical context and self-teacher generation. From swing-set reference, PhysOPSD constructs dual-level drafts (ddense, dabs) across paired variants varying only in initial angular velocity (0.12 vs. 1.7 rad/s). Conditioned on these drafts, the self-teacher faithfully synthesizes the corresponding motion dynamics. More case studies are in Figures 11 to 13. Privilege Construction. Experiments In this section, we conduct experiments to an- (RQ1) Does swer the following research questions: PhysOPSD improve physically plausible video generation? (RQ2) Does executable code provide effective (RQ3) How do structured privileged supervision? privileges improve learning? 5.1. Experimental Settings Baselines. We apply PhysOPSD to two unified video generators, OmniWeaving [30] and UniVideo [43]. As post-training method, our primary comparisons are against the respective base models to directly measure capability gains. Since prior physics-oriented posttraining methods are built on disparate backbones, we additionally implement three representative baseFigure 5. Qualitative results of PhysOPSD. More results are shown in Figures 14 to 17. lines: PhyT2V [45] for test-time scaling, SFT using WISA [42], and PhysHPO [5] for offline RL. We also report results from advanced video generators for reference, while further examining OPSD variants in our ablation studies. Details of baselines are in Section B. Evaluations. We evaluate PhysOPSD across two complementary aspects: ➀ physical plausibility, adopting VideoPhy-2 [3] for T2V and PhyGround [24] for TI2V to assess law-specific physical adherence; and ➁ general video quality, employing VBench [11] to measure general visual fidelity and semantic alignment. Implementation Details. PhysOPSD optimizes student LoRA parameters using AdamW with constant learning rate of 1 105, weight decay of 0.01, and gradient clipping at 1.0. Teacher weights are updated via an exponential moving average with decay of 0.9999 after paired gradient aggregation. Each student trajectory uses 𝐾 = 20 rollout denoising steps. Training employs BF16 mixed precision on NVIDIA H20 GPUs. At deployment, the student generates videos without teacher or simulation guidance. 5.2. Main Results To answer RQ1, we conduct comprehensive evaluations of PhysOPSD on physical and general generation benchmarks in Table 1, complemented by qualitative baseline comparisons (Figures 14 and 15) and diverse generative showcases (Figures 5, 16 and 17). Observations are summarized below: Obs.❶ PhysOPSD consistently improves physical plausibility across backbones with high sample efficiency, while preserving general video quality. As shown in Table 1, PhysOPSD achieves top physical adherence across both UniVideo (13B) and OmniWeaving (8.3B), boosting VideoPhy-2 overall scores by +4.2 and +4.1, and PhyGround by +1.6 and +3.4, respectively, with physical commonsense (PC) reaching 4.61. Crucially, PhysOPSD achieves these gains using only 3K samples, markedly outperforming SFT (80K) and offline RL (21K). Meanwhile, this physical specialization incurs no catastrophic forgetting: VBench confirms that PhysOPSD maintains or even slightly improves overall visual quality and text alignment (e.g., UniVideo rises from 83.5 to 84.0, while OmniWeaving 7 remains steady at 83.3), verifying that on-policy distillation protects foundational visual representations. Obs.❷ PhysOPSD generates physically faithful dynamics over baselines and generalizes robustly to visually rich, open-domain scenes. In Figures 14 and 15, baselines exhibit motion stagnation, severe geometric distortions, or broken reflection mechanics during concrete leveling and teapot rotation, whereas PhysOPSD synthesizes continuous, physically consistent interactions. Furthermore, although physical drafts in PhysOPSD-Engine use simplified simulation geometry, the learned dynamics transfer robustly to open-domain photorealistic scenes (Figures 5, 16 and 17), successfully capturing fluid sloshing, impact cratering, elastic penetration, and optical reflection. This verifies that PhysOPSD internalizes transferable physical mechanics rather than overfitting to synthetic simulation appearances. 5.3. Analysis of Code-as-Privilege To answer RQ2, we compare different privileged modalities under an identical budget of 3K samples, as shown in Figure 6: (i) vanilla model (w/o Privilege); (ii) declarative prompt expansion (w/ Refined Text); (iii) real reference videos (w/ Real Video); and (iv) executable simulation drafts (w/ Coding Draft). We give the following insights: Figure 6. Privilege context analysis. Executable coding drafts yield superior physical adherence over text and real videos. Obs.❸ Executable code serves as an effective privileged context for physically plausible video generation. As shown in Figure 6, refined text (w/ Refined Text) yields negligible physical gains and slightly decreases VideoPhy-2 All (62.8 vs. 62.9), showing that declarative descriptions cannot ground spatiotemporal mechanics. Meanwhile, real reference videos (w/ Real Video) produce only marginal improvements (63.1 vs. 62.9), as complex background and visual clutter encourage the teacher to rely on visual shortcuts rather than transferable dynamics. In contrast, PhysOPSD (w/ Coding Draft) achieves decisive improvements, boosting PhyGround Overall to 68.3 (+3.5 over real video) and VideoPhy-2 All to 67.0 (+3.9 over real video). As qualitatively shown in Fig8 ures 4 and 11 to 13, PhysOPSD isolates pure dynamics from visual noise and enables parametric control, empowering the self-teacher with dense, physically faithful supervision. 5.4. Analysis of Structured Privilege To answer RQ3, we further dissect the individual contributions of our two structural strategies under controlled budget of 3K samples: dual-level physical privilege and controlled physical variation. Performance gains over the base model on VideoPhy-2 are illustrated in Figure 7. We summarize the following observations: Figure 7. Structured physical privilege analysis. Both the stepped dual-level hierarchy and (Right) (Left) parameter-controlled paired variations consistently yield superior physical adherence over their uncoupled counterparts. Obs.❹ Dual-level privilege smooths knowledge transfer via an intermediate information bottleneck. In Figure 7 (Left), while Abstract-Only (+2.6 on All) lacks complete geometric constraints and Dense-Only (+3.4) encourages visual shortcuts, our stepped hierarchy (Dual-Level) attains the highest gain (+4.1 on All). This confirms that abstract drafts effectively bridge the privilege gap to enable progressive dynamic internalization. Obs.❺ Controlled physical variation exposes dynamic causality beyond learning from isolated scenes. In Figure 7 (Right), training on independent physical scenes without parameter-controlled variations (Independent-Only) achieves +3.3 gain on All. In contrast, structuring data into paired variants differing by single physical parameter (Controlled Pairs) elevates the gain to +4.1. This demonstrates that exposing explicit counterfactual dynamic shifts is far more effective for internalizing physical causality than merely observing standalone physical scenarios. 5.5. Analysis of Data Efficiency Finally, we examine the data efficiency and scaling behavior of PhysOPSD by varying the training data budget from 1K to 4K instances. Performance gains are illustrated in Figure 8: Obs.❻ PhysOPSD exhibits remarkable sample efficiency and steady scaling potential. As shown in Figure 8, with merely 1K samples, PhysOPSD yields Empowering Rather Than Replacing Generation. Central to our philosophy is leveraging coding agents to empower generative models rather than substituting them at test time. PhysOPSD-Engine is thus designed as an open, modular pipeline interfacing standard coding LLMs with physics engines. As foundational coding agents and physics solvers advance, the pipeline naturally inherits the ability to synthesize increasingly complex physical scenarios without altering the distillation formulation. Boundaries of Simulation-Groundable Dynamics. The physical scope of PhysOPSD is bounded by scenarios that standard simulation engines can stably compute: rigid-body contacts, elastic mechanics, and fluid dynamics. Chaotic multi-physics and thermodynamic phase transitions (e.g., combustion) are deliberately excluded due to solver instability and difficulty in isolating parameters. Rather than emulating all physical phenomena, our objective is establishing principled blueprint for internalizing physical dynamics via code privilege. Figure 8. Data scaling analysis. PhysOPSD delivers physical improvements even in low-data regimes and scales steadily. an immediate improvement of +1.6 on All (+1.8 on PC 4). As the dataset scales to 4K, overall gains steadily increase to +5.1 (+3.8 on SA 4 and +2.8 on PC 4) without premature plateauing. Compared to traditional paradigms requiring tens of thousands of samples (e.g., 80K for SFT and 21K for offline RL), PhysOPSD leverages dense on-policy supervision from structured code privileges, delivering high sample efficiency and sustainable scaling performance. 6. Conclusion In this work, we present PhysOPSD, post-training framework that introduces executable code as privileged physical context for on-policy self-distillation. Recognizing that executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability, we develop PhysOPSD-Engine to construct verifiable simulation scenes and rendered drafts. PhysOPSD systematically translates these properties into dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose dynamic causality. Extensive experiments on standard physics benchmarks demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones with high sample efficiency, while preserving general video quality. We hope our code-as-privilege inspires future research on leveraging coding agents to empower generative models rather than replacing them, advancing physically grounded visual generation. 7. Scope of This Report PhysOPSD conAlgorithm over Monolithic Models. tributes general on-policy self-distillation framework rather than delivering single weight-locked model. This motivates our focus on relative capability gains over respective base generators (e.g., UniVideo [43] and OmniWeaving [30]) to confirm crossarchitecture generalizability. Furthermore, our compact default budget of 3K samples highlights sample efficiency, while our scaling analysis (Section 5.5) confirms steady performance gains as data increases.

PhysOPSD-Engine Details Synthesizing executable physical scenes requires translating abstract dynamic descriptions into syntactically valid and numerically stable simulation code. While frontier LLMs/VLMs exhibit proficient code generation and spatial reasoning, the non-linear nature of contact dynamics makes single-pass zeroshot generation unreliable for complex physical phenomena. To guarantee verifiable physical basis, PhysOPSD-Engine combines frontier coding agent with an automated execution-guided refinement loop. Iterative Scene Refinement Workflow. We adopt GPT-6-Astra as the backbone coding agent. Upon generating an initial scene program P, PhysOPSD-Engine executes it in the target backend (e.g., MuJoCo [39] or Blender [4]) and aggregates diagnostic feedback across three modalities: ❶ execution logs (e.g., syntax errors or solver convergence warnings), ❷ kinematic telemetry (e.g., penetration anomalies or constraint forces), and ❸ rendered preview keyframes. When physical implausibility, solver divergence, or poor camera observability is detected, the coding agent inspects the diagnostic trace to revise geometric configurations, contact parameters, or camera trajectories. This execution-observation-revision cycle iterates until all four verification criteria in Section 4.2 are satisfied. Multi-Level Draft Generation. To prevent dynamic discrepancies across privilege levels, dense drafts ddense and abstract drafts dabs for given variant are rendered from an identical, frozen simulation state trajectory. Specifically, once simulation execution succeeds, PhysOPSD-Engine records the full kinematic trajectory of all bodies and contact events. ddense is rendered with full surface meshes, material shaders, and realistic lighting, whereas dabs renders simplified wireframe primitives and centroid trajectories from the exact same camera viewpoint. This trajectory freezing guarantees that both privilege levels share identical underlying dynamics, completely eliminating confounding dynamic drift caused by resimulation. For controlled variants, non-target attributes and initial conditions are frozen to isolate the causal parameter shift. Outcome-Grounded Dual Prompt Annotation. In the main text, we denote the target text condition uniformly as for mathematical clarity. In practice, accommodating our omni-capable video generator entails producing two complementary text conditions via Qwen3-VL-32B [46], conditioned on the dense draft alongside structured fact card containing measured physical telemetry: Figure 9. Comparison of PhysOPSD-Engine vs. CodexHarness. T2V Prompt: self-contained description detailing the scene context, physical conditions, observable dynamic trajectory, and final state, used for deployment-time text-only student generation. V2V Instruction: an imperative prompt instructing the model to perform photorealistic visual refinement while strictly preserving the underlying spatiotemporal dynamics and spatial layout, shared by the teacher and draft-conditioned student. Both text modalities are grounded strictly in the executed simulation telemetry rather than speculative prior descriptions. The concrete system prompts utilized for annotation are detailed below. Effectiveness of PhysOPSD-Engine To further validate the necessity of our agentic execution-guided loop, we compare PhysOPSD-Engine against standard harness framework (i.e., Codex) using the identical backbone coding model (GPT-6-Astra). As illustrated in Figure 9, naive code generation without closed-loop simulation feedback frequently degenerates into non-physical shortcuts: collapsing into 2D schematic toy drawings without fluid mechanics (e.g., fluid pouring), omitting structural apparatus and floating in an ungrounded void (e.g., sponge

sections.title: System Prompt for Dual Prompt Annotation
sections.content: """ You are an expert video annotation assistant specializing in physical dynamics , object interactions , and temporally grounded video descriptions . Your task is to generate accurate training prompts for text - to - video ( T2V ) generation and video - to - video ( V2V ) editing . You are given two videos representing different physical settings of the same scene , together with chronological visual observations and verified fact card . Treat them as independent physical outcomes , not as before - and - after sequence . Prioritize factual accuracy , physical consistency , and temporal grounding over narrative richness . 1. VISUAL AND PHYSICAL GROUNDING - Identify the principal objects , initial configuration , physical interactions , motion progression , and actual final states . - Examine the full temporal sequence . Compare the first and last frames to distinguish temporary deformation from permanent changes , motion from detachment , and partial events from completed events . - Describe observed dynamics rather than expected textbook outcomes . Changing physical parameter does not guarantee specific result . - Use the verified fact card to identify physical conditions , affected objects , measured states , and camera settings . Ground the actual motion and outcomes in the provided visual evidence . - Do not infer screen - space directions from numerical coordinates . Motion alone does not establish collision , fracture , or detachment . - Distinguish physical quantities accurately , including friction , damping , mass , stiffness , and velocity . Do not confuse physical speed with video playback speed . - Omit uncertain details rather than inventing events or outcomes . 2. ANNOTATION REQUIREMENTS Generate two English training descriptions for EACH physical variant . . T2V Prompt ( t2v_prompt ) : Write self - contained target - video description , normally 70 -115 words , including : - Principal objects , geometry , spatial layout , and realistic appearance . - Relevant qualitative physical conditions and affected objects . - Actual motion , key interactions , and observed final outcomes . - Camera viewpoint and scene composition . The description must stand alone without referring to the source video , simulation , editing process , or the other variant . . V2V Instruction ( v2v_ins truction ) : Write concise appearance - editing instruction , normally 35 -65 words , using two sentences : - Begin with " Convert this video into photorealistic live - action footage of ..." to specify realistic objects , materials , and appearance . - Begin the second sentence with " Preserve ..." to maintain the physical conditions , motion dynamics , event sequence , final outcome , timing , spatial arrangement , and camera behavior . The SAME V2V instruction must be used for both dense and abstract video representations of the same physical variant . 3. CONSISTENCY CONSTRAINTS - Keep target materials and non - intervened scene attributes consistent across variants and between T2V and V2V descriptions . - Preserve actual objects , apparatus , supports , containers , openings , and spatial relationships . Distinguish transparent containers from their liquid contents where applicable . - Do not introduce unobserved objects , people , backgrounds , equipment , or physical events . Do not copy arbitrary proxy colors or textures . - Respect the verified camera configuration . Changes in framing do not necessarily indicate camera motion . - Do not include raw numerical coefficients , measurement units , variable names , pixel dimensions , or simulator - specific terminology in the training descriptions . Physical object counts are allowed . - Describe each variant independently . Avoid relative expressions such as " faster than the other video "; describe its actual behavior instead . - Ground descriptions in the CURRENT executed outcome , not in an original reference caption or an assumed physical result . 4. OUTPUT FORMAT ... 5. FINAL VERIFICATION ... PhysOPSD-3K comprises 3K total encompassing base executable scenes instances, alongside their derived multi-abstraction drafts (ddense, dabs) and parameter-controlled paired variants (d𝑎, d𝑏). These results confirm that code-derived privileges effectively isolate dynamic mechanics from visual noise, providing transferable physical guidance without appearance shortcuts. A.3.
